decisions.reason: The coded-referral allocation remains a separate four-ticket rule, and its same-message MODIFY already records the accepted value.
Changing no-referral ticket quantity does not alter the coded-referral commission; the accepted $35 amount is already recorded separately at the same message.
The source changes the no-referral ticket quantity, not the separate $12 commission rule, which already has its own same-message MODIFY.
Ticket quantity after an omitted referral does not change which referral identifiers are valid or the prohibition on self-referrals.
The six-ticket no-referral allocation does not change an NFT's token-serial referral identity, persistence, or display locations.
The current FAQ attributes do not encode a no-referral ticket quantity; their one-ticket language concerns successful coded referrals and is not changed by this source Event.
Changing how many tickets a no-referral mint creates does not change whether active tickets and other NFT properties follow the NFT after transfer.
The landing-page state describes coded-referral marketing and layout and contains no no-referral ticket quantity that must change.
Increasing tickets issued by a no-referral mint does not change the prize amount, winner count, eligibility method, draw trigger, or pool allocation.

The metadata Requirement remains unchanged: it must display accurate ticket and earnings data. Message 688 reports an execution failure already represented in its history, not a new metadata value rule.
The About-page state mentions no-code ticket allocation only generically and does not specify a quantity contradicted by the six-ticket rule.
The source changes ticket issuance quantity, not Small Block ticket eligibility, reset behavior, or carry-forward semantics.
